_meta.purpose: One chronological spine for ancient India — the connective tissue that threads together everything the atlas holds about the deep past. Each era is read on five facets at once: the LANGUAGE spoken, the SCRIPT it was written in (if any), the PEOPLE (what ancient DNA says about who was here), the RULERS/POLITY, and the HERITAGE they left. Every era is a doorway into a deeper page (scripts, the Vedas, Ashoka, the DNA record, the heritage atlas).
_meta.honesty: The established-vs-contested discipline used across the atlas. Dates for deep prehistory are ranges, not points, and are labelled. A GENETIC finding (well-supported) is kept separate from a HISTORICAL interpretation (often contested) — the 'Aryan migration' framing especially. Where a script is UNREAD (Indus) or a language is RECONSTRUCTED (Proto-Dravidian, PIE) we say so; we don't dress inference as fact.
_meta.facets: language · script · people (DNA) · rulers/polity · heritage · events

interrogation.why: History is not a neutral download of ‘what happened’ — it is what SURVIVED, who was allowed to write it, and who benefited from the version that lasted. So every fact here also carries: how we know it (evidence tier), how solid the claim is (confidence), WHO recorded it, and whether the record was shaped by the winner/power of the time. Click any fact to interrogate it. The point is not to make you doubt everything equally — a sequenced genome and a temple you can stand in are not a court poet's flattery — but to make the DIFFERENCE visible.

primary.label: Primary / physical
primary.note: Direct physical evidence read by modern method: a sequenced genome, a carved inscription, an excavated city. The hardest kind — though still interpreted.

peer-reviewed.label: Peer-reviewed
peer-reviewed.note: A published scientific finding others have checked (e.g. the ancient-DNA papers). Strong, but a live field that can revise.

contemporary-text.label: Contemporary text
contemporary-text.note: Written at the time by someone who was there — powerful, but ALWAYS from someone's point of view (a king's edict is also propaganda).

later-text.label: Later account
later-text.note: Written generations or centuries after, often by the tradition that ‘won’. Useful, but the most exposed to shaping and legend.

reference.label: Reference / tertiary
reference.note: An encyclopaedia or textbook summary (e.g. Wikipedia). Convenient, but a digest of other sources — verify against the primaries.

inference.label: Reconstruction / inference
inference.note: Not directly attested at all — rebuilt by method (comparative linguistics for Proto-languages, models for unsampled ancestry). Honest, but a hypothesis.

confidence.debated: Genuinely open among specialists; competing readings.
confidence.contested: Disputed, and often politically charged — read the ⚠ note.

interrogation.shaping: ‘Recorded by’ names WHO left the trace; ‘shaped by’ names the power/interest that could bend it. When these two differ from ‘what a neutral observer would record’, that gap IS the winner's-history problem.

sources.label: Ancient-DNA population shifts (this atlas): Narasimhan et al. 2019, Shinde et al. 2019
Vedic period; Mahajanapadas; Maurya Empire; Gupta Empire — Wikipedia

eras.name: Deep prehistory — the substrate

language.detail: No records. The deep population — the AASI (Ancient Ancestral South Indians) — is the substrate every later group mixed into.

people.detail: A deeply divergent lineage, distantly related to the Andamanese; the foundational layer of South Asian ancestry.

evidence.recorded_by: modern population geneticists (inferred, not directly sampled)
evidence.shaped_by: none ancient — but a POLITICALLY charged topic today
evidence.how: No ancient AASI genome has been sequenced yet; AASI is a statistical source-population inferred in every model of South Asian ancestry (Narasimhan/Reich). So: strong consensus, but a reconstruction, not a body in a lab.

heritage.detail: Some of the oldest human traces in the subcontinent.

evidence.how: Physical remains you can still see at Bhimbetka; dating by stratigraphy and style. About as unmediated as evidence gets — nobody's ‘winner’ curated it.

events: AASI lineage established as the substrate

eras.name: Indus (Harappan) Civilisation

language.detail: We cannot name the language family — the script is undeciphered. Some argue an early Dravidian; unproven.

script.detail: Short seal-inscriptions; never read, and not even confirmed to be full writing. A minority view makes it Brahmi's ancestor — separated by a ~1500-year gap.

evidence.shaped_by: MODERN politics — nationalist vs colonial readings
evidence.how: The marks are physically real and primary; but ‘what they SAY’ is unknown — undeciphered. Claims that it's early Dravidian, or the parent of Brahmi, are contested and often carry a modern political charge. Here the primary object is solid but every INTERPRETATION is a hypothesis.

people.detail: The one sequenced IVC genome (Rakhigarhi) was exactly this mix — with NO Steppe and NO Anatolian-farmer ancestry.

evidence.recorded_by: Shinde et al. 2019 (Cell) — the Rakhigarhi genome
evidence.shaped_by: n=1, so read with care; the finding itself is not ‘shaped’
evidence.how: A single ancient genome, sequenced and peer-reviewed. Powerful and hard to spin — but it IS one individual, and the authors say so. Strong evidence, honestly bounded.

rulers.detail: Remarkably uniform cities (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira) with no palaces or grand tombs — governance still debated.

evidence.recorded_by: the archaeological record (absence of palaces/royal tombs)
evidence.shaped_by: none ancient — but ‘absence of evidence’ is slippery
evidence.how: We infer ‘no kings’ from what's MISSING — no palaces, no royal graves, no army art. That's a reasonable read of primary excavation, but an argument from silence: a very different footing from a genome or an inscription.

heritage.text: Planned cities, the Great Bath, standardised weights, drainage
heritage.detail: Among the most sophisticated urban planning of the Bronze Age.

events: Gradual decline ~1900 BCE (climate/river shifts, not a proven invasion)

eras.name: The Vedic period

language.detail: An Indo-European language — kin to Persian, Greek, Latin. Composed and transmitted ORALLY for centuries.

evidence.recorded_by: the priestly (Brahmin) composers of the hymns
evidence.shaped_by: a PRIESTLY elite — this is the canon of one class
evidence.how: The language is known from the Vedas themselves — an extraordinary oral text preserved almost verbatim. But it is the voice of a ritual elite; the speech of everyone else (labourers, the conquered, women, the ‘dasa’) survives only through that filter. What we ‘know’ of the age is largely what the priests chose to chant.

script.text: None at first — oral, then later Brahmi
script.detail: The Vedas were memorised, not written, for a very long time. Sanskrit had no script of its own.

evidence.recorded_by: the oral tradition (memory), written down much later
evidence.shaped_by: transmission by memory = control by the reciters
evidence.how: That the age was pre-literate is inferred from the absence of Vedic-era writing and the tradition's own oral method. Reliable — but note the whole record depended on WHO was permitted to memorise and recite it.

people.detail: Steppe pastoralist ancestry entered NW South Asia ~2000–1500 BCE — the same pulse that reshaped Bronze-Age Europe. The genetics are not disputed.

evidence.recorded_by: Narasimhan et al. 2019 (Science) — the Swat Valley time-transect
evidence.shaped_by: the GENETICS aren't shaped; the ‘Aryan’ NARRATIVE around them is fiercely contested
evidence.how: Here is the cleanest split in the whole timeline. That Steppe ancestry arrived ~2000–1500 BCE is peer-reviewed and NOT seriously disputed. What it MEANS — ‘Aryan invasion’, peaceful migration, or (some argue) an out-of-India origin — is a HISTORICAL interpretation, politically loaded, and genuinely contested. We hold the finding as established and flag the story as contested. ⚠

rulers.detail: Pastoral, then settling agricultural societies along the Sapta-Sindhu and Ganga-Yamuna doab.

evidence.shaped_by: victors' hymns — battles are told from one side
evidence.how: The famous ‘Battle of the Ten Kings’ and the raja lineages come from the Rigveda itself — i.e. from the side that composed the hymn. Classic winner's account: the defeated (e.g. the ‘Dasa/Dasyu’) are described only by their enemies.

heritage.detail: The Rigveda — among the oldest religious texts still in use; the Nāsadīya Sūkta (Hymn of Creation) sits here.

evidence.shaped_by: the surviving canon = what one tradition preserved
evidence.how: The Vedas are a genuine, astonishingly well-preserved primary text OF THEIR KIND. But ‘heritage’ here is textual, not material — and it's the heritage the Vedic tradition kept. What rival or folk traditions of the age believed is largely lost.

events: The ‘Aryan migration’ interpretation — genetics established, historical narrative CONTESTED
Shift east into the Gangetic plain

eras.name: The Mahajanapadas & the śramaṇa age

language.detail: The everyday Middle Indo-Aryan vernaculars — the real bridge to the modern languages — rise beside formal Sanskrit.

script.detail: After the long post-Indus gap, writing returns; Brahmi is taking shape, ready for the Mauryan state.

people.detail: The two ancestral populations (Ancestral North & South Indians) mix in two directions; almost all South Asians today are a blend of them.

rulers.detail: Republics (gaṇa-saṅghas) and kingdoms; Magadha grows dominant under the Haryanka/Nanda dynasties.

evidence.shaped_by: religious traditions writing their own founding era
evidence.how: The list of ‘16 great realms’ and their kings comes largely from Buddhist/Jain texts and later Puranic king-lists — written by the traditions that grew powerful, often centuries after. Real, but a later account, not contemporary record.

heritage.detail: The Buddha and Mahavira teach in this age — a philosophical revolution that will shape the whole of Asia.

evidence.recorded_by: the Buddhist & Jain communities (canon written later)
evidence.shaped_by: the sanghas that survived preserved their own founders
evidence.how: That the Buddha and Mahavira lived and taught in this window is broadly accepted, but the biographies were written down generations later by devotees — reverent accounts, not neutral chronicle.

events: Second urbanisation of the Ganga plain

eras.name: The Mauryan Empire — Ashoka

language.text: Prakrit (state), Sanskrit, Greek & Aramaic on the frontier
language.detail: The edicts speak in Prakrit at the core and switch to Greek/Aramaic on the Hellenistic edge — the multilingual reach of the empire.

script.detail: The first securely readable Indian script. Brahmi in the core, Kharoshthi in the northwest — deciphered only in 1837 (Prinsep).

evidence.recorded_by: the Mauryan state (carved), read by Prinsep 1837
evidence.shaped_by: the state chose what to carve — but the OBJECT is unforgeable
evidence.how: The inscriptions are primary, physical and datable; the decipherment is well-established. Among the strongest evidence in the timeline — you can go touch the stone. (What it says is the state's message; that it exists and says it, is fact.)

people.detail: The caste system begins to reduce inter-group mixing, ‘freezing’ ancestry proportions — itself readable in later DNA.

evidence.recorded_by: modern DNA (endogamy dated by later genomes)
evidence.shaped_by: none — a genetic signal, not a written claim
evidence.how: The onset of strong endogamy is dated genetically (Reich lab). It's an inference from modern/ancient DNA, not from any text — so it sidesteps the winner's-history filter entirely.

rulers.detail: One of the largest ancient empires — from Afghanistan to Karnataka. We can VERIFY Ashoka's rule from his own edicts.

evidence.recorded_by: Ashoka himself (the edicts) + later Buddhist chronicles
evidence.shaped_by: the KING himself — the edicts are self-portrait AND propaganda
evidence.how: Rare luxury: a ruler's OWN words survive, datable and empire-wide — so his reign is verifiable, not legend. BUT the edicts are also PR: ‘what he said’ (remorse, dhamma) is his chosen image, and must be kept apart from later hagiography (Ashokavadana) that turned him monster-to-saint. Strong evidence, read as self-portrait.

heritage.text: The Edicts, the pillars, the Lion Capital (now India's emblem)
heritage.detail: Rock & pillar edicts across the empire; the Sarnath lion capital.

evidence.how: Physical, standing, datable — the surest kind. Note that monumental heritage always over-represents the powerful: we have the emperor's pillars, not the villages.

events: The Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse (Rock Edict 13)
State patronage of dhamma / Buddhism spreads

eras.name: Post-Mauryan to the Gupta ‘classical’ age

language.text: Classical Sanskrit codified; Prakrits flourish; Old Tamil in the south
language.detail: Pāṇini's grammar fixes Classical Sanskrit; in the Dravidian south, Old Tamil produces the Sangam literature — a parallel, unrelated tradition.

script.text: Brahmi diversifies → Gupta script; Tamil-Brahmi in the south
script.detail: ‘Late Brahmi’ (Gupta) is the hinge from which Devanagari and the northern scripts will grow; Tamil-Brahmi carries the Dravidian south.

people.text: The settled blend of modern South Asians
people.detail: Ancestry proportions much as today; regional communities distinct.

rulers.text: Shungas, Satavahanas, Kushanas, then the Guptas
rulers.detail: The Gupta era is remembered as a ‘golden age’ of science, maths (the decimal/zero), art and literature.

evidence.shaped_by: the very phrase ‘golden age’ is a court-and-later gloss
evidence.how: Gupta kings are well-attested by coins and inscriptions (primary). But ‘golden age’ is partly the Guptas' own court panegyric (e.g. the Allahabad praśasti of Samudragupta — literally a poem praising the king) and partly later nostalgia. The dynasty is fact; the glow is curated.

heritage.text: Ajanta & Ellora, Sanchi, Sangam poetry, Kalidasa, Aryabhata
heritage.detail: Rock-cut cave temples, classical drama, and the mathematics that gave the world the decimal place-value system.

evidence.shaped_by: elite patronage decided what got built & copied
evidence.how: Ajanta's paintings, Aryabhata's treatise, Kalidasa's plays survive as primary works. Rock-hard evidence they existed — though what survived is what wealthy patrons funded and later scribes chose to recopy.

events: Gupta ‘golden age’; Aryabhata; the concept of zero
